title: Zelensky declares a state of emergency in Ukraine's energy sector
body:
On 14 January 2026, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky declared a state of emergency in Ukraine's energy sector, with a particular focus on the capital, Kyiv. The decision followed Russian attacks on energy infrastructure that left residents of Kyiv without electricity, heating and water during subzero temperatures. According to the Kyiv Independent, Russian strikes had left about 70 percent of the capital without power on 13 January.

Under the emergency measures, a task force was created in Kyiv to coordinate the response around the clock. Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal, who had recently taken up the post, was assigned to lead efforts to support citizens and communities. Zelensky also ordered a review of the midnight curfew, which has been in place since martial law began at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, so that people could reach so-called "invincibility points" that provide power and heat. Authorities said Kyiv planned to add more of these points.

The government said it would seek equipment and electricity imports from foreign partners, and the Education Ministry and local authorities were asked to propose how children would attend school during the emergency. DTEK, Ukraine's largest private energy company, welcomed the measures. Repair crews were reported to be working in icy conditions and running short of replacement equipment.
